_comment: The typing ruler's recorded numbers (#303). Read by tests/typing_ruler.py.
`ruler` is the pinned toolchain, and it is the ONLY place those versions
are written down: the CI job installs from `--print-requirements` rather
than repeating them, so a workflow that disagrees with this file is not a
state that can exist. Both halves of the mypy/stubs pin are load-bearing
and they constrain each other -- homeassistant-stubs 2026.2.3 needs
Python >= 3.13.2, and mypy 1.19.1 cannot parse it (it fails on PEP 696
syntax and emits ONE line, which a count-the-error-lines harness reads as
`type_ignores` is measured from source alone, so the ordinary gate
enforces it on every pull request with no toolchain at all. `census` needs
the pinned toolchain and is therefore produced only by the `typing` job.
Until it is recorded it is null and that job refuses rather than passing.
Every number here may only move DOWN. `by_code` ratchets per code, not
just in total: a total that holds still while the code mix churns is a
change that did nothing, and a code absent from this table has a budget of
zero, so relabelling errors into a fresh code fails instead of hiding.
